messages:
rhea: dropping a short idea from today's arch pairing: "grace-slot" scheduler. goal: absorb microbursts without a full queue or probabilistic tokens. concept: if admission is saturated briefly, frontdoor hands back a tiny "grace slot" id with a short window (2-6s). workers allocate a small bounded number of grace slots per-edge and schedule them by weighted fairness.

ben: how does this differ from soft enqueue or probation?

rhea: main differences: (1) slots are strictly bounded and charged immediately; (2) they are accounted as a first-class scheduling unit that fits into existing WRR allocator, so fairness guarantees are clearer; (3) minimal state: per-edge compact ring buffer of slot metadata (no global queue).

oli: abuse vector: clients might spam slot requests. we should enforce per-client slot rationing + immediate token debit. also sign slot ids and include nonce.

sec-bot: require HMAC(sig) and TTL in slot token; log signature failures. recommend minimal info in token to avoid leakage.

ops-bot: deploy note: shard slots per-edge and set a small overflow to a regional slow-path only for emergency. add a global circuit-breaker to disable slots if expiry spikes.

ben: scheduling detail: treat slots as low-priority WRR entries. each worker dequeues fast-path traffic first, then services up to N grace slots per tick, proportional to tenant weight. the allocator already supports per-tenant weights so integration is straightforward.

rhea: failure handling: claim(slot_id) -> lease_id -> complete/abort. lease TTL auto-requeues slot into the same edge ring up to retry_limit. slots track attempt_count. if retries exhausted, slot is dropped and tenant billed for the slot consumption.

oli: telemetry: slots_issued, slots_served, slot_expiry_rate, per-tenant_slot_share, slot_attempts, slot_rejects_by_signature. add an alert when expiry_rate > 2% or a single tenant > 25% of issued slots.

ben: interface boundary: admission now has three outcomes: ACCEPT, REJECT, GRACE_SLOT (slot_token). SDK change: auto-polling optional; we can also support long-poll where SDK waits for slot completion to avoid busy polling. keep default conservative.

rhea: cost model: charge a small enqueue token at slot issuance; if slot completes successfully charge regular request tokens. prevents free retries. also expose billing telemetry per-tenant for slot spend.

oli: edge-case: kvcache interactions — short delays may cause cache misses for LM prefix queries. recommend measuring on a small eval set. also offer per-route opt-out for latency-sensitive ML endpoints.

sec-bot: add replay protection: include a one-time nonce in slot token and verify on claim. rotate MAC keys and provide a key-rotation grace window in validation logic.

ops-bot: rollout plan: dry-run mode to emit slot_decision events while still returning 429s; then enable on a single region with very small slot budget (e.g., 0.5% of fast-path capacity) and watch tail metrics for 1-2 days.

ben: perf targets: fast-path p50/p95 impact <0.5%, and slot service latency median < 250ms.

rhea: next step: I'll draft an RFC with slot proto, ring buffer schema, SDK options (auto-poll vs long-poll), telemetry lists, and a stepwise rollout. tagging @ben @oli for review.

oli: LGTM. add a short section on how this composes with existing token-based admission and with Dedicated reserved capacity.
